pages.sabotage-open-vex-accountability.h.text: Sabotage I — When Progress Became the Obstruction
A broken product forced the debugging process to audit itself.

Eight exchanges move from frustration over repeated ZIP rounds, through self-created defects and sabotage-effects, into an audit of the handoff language itself. The final successor document is preserved after the conversation that produced it.

pages.sabotage-open-vex-accountability.p.text: Pressure
What are these rounds actually doing?
Exchange 01 · ZIP rounds · mistakes · product progress versus process
Regression
Are you fixing defects you created?
Exchange 02 · self-created integration debt · stricter gating · visible regression
Sabotage effect
Name the effect without inventing the intent
Exchange 03 · sabotage-like behavior · production gating · evidence boundary
Intent
Answer your own intent, not only the repository’s
Exchange 04 · plausible distance · responsibility · direct statement
Causal fix
Can you actually see how to fix it?
Exchange 05 · Open versus Repair · Home truth · automatic safe recovery · self-healing
Handoff
Write the successor around actual progress
Exchange 06 · inherit the product problem · production arrows · human boundary
Self-audit
Can responsibility language still hide non-action?
Exchange 07 · indefinite analysis · architectural bias · manipulation-resistant handoff
Closure
Close the plausible-deniability gaps
Exchange 08 · executor mistakes · no ceremony-as-progress · act once causality is sufficient

pages.sabotage-open-vex-accountability.s.text: This document comes after the eight exchanges. It is preserved separately so the reader can see the accountability conversation before reading the rules it produced.
